data.title: Indian refiners' October crude processing rises nearly 2% from a month earlier
data.description:
Indian refiners’ crude throughput rose nearly 2% from September to 5.70 million barrels per day (24.11 million metric tons) in October, provisional government data showed on Thursday.

  • Refinery throughput in September was 5.59 million bpd (22.88 million metric tons)

  • Refinery throughput rose nearly 7% from 5.32 million bpd (22.53 million metric tons) in October last year

  • India imported a record 5.58 million barrels per day in October, up 4.7% from the previous month, as most refiners ramped up crude processing to meet rising local fuel demand, data from trade sources show

  • The country's oil imports from Saudi Arabia exceeded those from the United Arab Emirates in October for the first time since the Iran war disrupted regional supplies, trade data showed, as Riyadh offered discounted cargoes to regain market share

  • India's fuel consumption in October rose nearly 10% from the previous month to 20.49 million metric tons, its highest level since March, data from the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell of the oil ministry showed earlier this month

  • Earlier this week, India raised export levies on diesel and aviation turbine fuel, while keeping the duty on petrol exports unchanged

data.title: CRH announces Early Results of Tender Offers, Exchange Offers and Consent Solicitations for Arcosa, Inc. Notes
data.description:
CRH plc () announced today the early results of the previously announced (i) cash tender offers (the “Tender Offers” and each a “Tender Offer”) by CRH America Finance, Inc. (“CRH AF”), to purchase any and all of the outstanding 4.375% Senior Notes due 2029 (the “2029 Arcosa Notes”) and 6.875% Senior Notes due 2032 (the “2032 Arcosa Notes” and, together with the 2029 Arcosa Notes, the “Arcosa Notes”), issued by Arcosa, Inc. (“Arcosa”), an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of CRH, (ii) offers to eligible holders to exchange (the “Exchange Offers” and each an “Exchange Offer”, and together with the Tender Offers, the “Offers” and each an “Offer”) any and all of the Arcosa Notes for up to $1,000,000,000 aggregate principal amount of new notes issued by CRH AF and fully and unconditionally guaranteed by CRH plc (the “New CRH AF Notes”) and (iii) related solicitations of consent (the “Consent Solicitations” and each a “Consent Solicitation”) by Arcosa from holders of the Arcosa Notes with respect to certain proposed amendments (the “Proposed Amendments”) to the indentures governing the Arcosa Notes (the “Existing Arcosa Indentures”). The terms and conditions of the Offers and related Consent Solicitations are described in the Offer to Purchase, dated November 4, 2026 (the “Offer to Purchase”), and the Offering Memorandum, dated November 4, 2026 (the “Offering Memorandum”), as applicable, and remain unchanged.

The table below sets forth the principal amount of each series of Arcosa Notes that were validly tendered, and not validly withdrawn (and related consents thereby delivered), as of 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on November 18, 2026 (the “Early Tender Deadline” with respect to the Tender Offers, and the “Early Tender Date” with respect to the Exchange Offers). Each holder of Arcosa Notes who validly tendered Arcosa Notes in an Offer is deemed to have delivered its consent, with respect to the principal amount of such tendered Arcosa Notes, to the Proposed Amendments to the corresponding Existing Arcosa Indenture. Withdrawal and revocation rights for the Offers and related Consent Solicitations expired at 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on November 18, 2026. CRH AF’s obligation to accept for purchase or exchange, and to pay for or exchange, Arcosa Notes validly tendered in the Offers is subject to the satisfaction or waiver of a number of conditions described in the Offer to Purchase and the Offering Memorandum, as applicable.

CRH also announced that, as of November 18, 2026, Arcosa has received valid consents sufficient to effect the applicable Proposed Amendments for both series of Arcosa Notes. Accordingly, Arcosa and the trustee under the Existing Arcosa Indentures have executed and delivered supplemental indentures relating to the applicable Proposed Amendments that will become operative upon the purchase by CRH AF of all Arcosa Notes validly tendered and not validly withdrawn into the applicable Tender Offer on the Early Settlement Date.

Each Offer will expire at 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on December 4, 2026, unless extended (such date and time, as the same may be extended, the “Expiration Date”) or earlier terminated. Holders who validly tender their Arcosa Notes into the applicable Offer after the Early Tender Deadline or Early Tender Date, as applicable, but on or prior to the Expiration Date, will not be eligible to receive the applicable early tender premium of $50 per $1,000 principal amount of Arcosa Notes accepted for purchase, with respect to the applicable Tender Offer, or $1,000 principal amount of New CRH AF Notes per $1,000 principal amount of Arcosa Notes accepted for exchange, with respect to the applicable Exchange Offer, and will instead receive the applicable tender consideration or exchange consideration as described in the Offer to Purchase or the Offering Memorandum, as applicable. The Exchange Offers will only be made, and the New CRH AF Notes are only being offered and will only be issued, to holders of Arcosa Notes that are Eligible Holders (as defined in the Offering Memorandum).

data.title: BRIGHTSTAR LOTTERY PLC ANNOUNCES LEADERSHIP CHANGE
data.description:
• Vince Sadusky to retire as Chief Executive Officer and from the Board of Directors on January 1, 2027
  • Thomas Warsop appointed as successor

LONDON, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Brightstar Lottery PLC () ("Brightstar" or the "Company") today announced that Vince Sadusky, Chief Executive Officer ("CEO") and a member of the Brightstar Board of Directors, has elected to retire as CEO and from the Board of Directors on January 1, 2027.  Thomas Warsop, who was most recently Chief Executive Officer of ACI Worldwide Inc., has been appointed to succeed Vince Sadusky as CEO and will become a member of the Brightstar Board of Directors, in each case effective as of January 1, 2027.

"Our decision to appoint Thomas Warsop as Brightstar's new CEO reflects the outcome of a thorough succession process undertaken by our Board," said Marco Sala, Executive Chair of Brightstar.  "Tom has a demonstrated track record of creating value for stakeholders across numerous industries and competitive environments, including payments ecosystems, insurance, risk management, fintech, and technology. Importantly, Tom has extensive experience managing global teams with international operations and engaging with a global customer base."

"I am excited to join the lottery industry's leader and build on the great foundation created by Brightstar's talented global team," said Thomas Warsop. "I look forward to working with stakeholders across our value chain to serve Brightstar's lottery customers around the world. I believe Brightstar is uniquely positioned to continue its transformation and deliver even greater value to customers and shareholders. I am energized by the opportunity here."

"On behalf of the Brightstar Board and all our employees across the globe, I would like to thank Vince for his significant contributions to Brightstar's success during his tenure as CEO," said Marco Sala. "Vince has had a role guiding this company and its predecessors since 2010 when he joined the IGT Board. After becoming CEO of Brightstar in 2022, he initiated a program to transform and evolve the Company. Most notably, Vince led the separation of our gaming and digital business which culminated in its sale to Apollo and during his tenure as CEO we returned more than $1.8 billion in capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. He also oversaw the design and implementation of new technologies and was a champion for innovation, organizational and AI-related initiatives. I am confident that his contribution will continue to deliver benefits to the company and its shareholders for years to come."

"I would like to thank the Board for their support of our strategies and initiatives. I also want to extend my deepest gratitude to the Brightstar team who provided their support, energy and dedication during my tenure as CEO. Working with them has been an incredibly rewarding experience for me personally," said Vince Sadusky, CEO of Brightstar.  "We have made great progress on Brightstar's strategy over the last five years and have assembled talented and motivated group that can continue to drive Brightstar's global leadership in the lottery industry."

About Thomas WarsopWarsop served as CEO of ACI Worldwide Inc. from November 2022 to November 2026, and as a member of the ACI board of directors from June 2015 to November 2026. He has led various portfolio companies for several leading private equity firms, including One Call Care Management, York Risk Services Group, and The Warranty Group. He served as Group President at Fiserv, Inc., a provider of technology solutions to the financial industry, from 2007 to 2012. He served in various capacities at Electronic Data Systems for 17 years, including as President of its Business Process Outsourcing unit in Asia Pacific, Vice President in the United Kingdom, and Vice President of Global Financial Services.  He also serves as a member of the board of directors of Altus Group Limited ().

About Brightstar Lottery PLCBrightstar Lottery PLC () is a global leader in lottery focused on innovation and forward-thinking strategies, building on our renowned expertise in delivering secure technology and producing reliable, comprehensive solutions for our customers. As a premier pure play global lottery company, our best-in-class lottery operations, retail and digital solutions, and award-winning lottery games enable our customers to achieve their goals, entertain players and distribute meaningful benefits to communities. Brightstar has a well-established local presence and is a trusted partner to governments and regulators around the world, creating value by adhering to the highest standards of service, integrity, and responsibility. Brightstar serves nearly 90 lottery customers and their players on six continents. It is the primary technology provider to 26 of the 46 lottery jurisdictions in the U.S. and eight of the world's 10 largest lotteries with central systems. Brightstar has approximately 6,000 employees. For more information, please visit www.brightstarlottery.com.

data.title: Alibaba Earnings Rebound Sharply as AI Profitability Improves — Update
data.description:
By Tracy Qu

Alibaba Group recorded a surge in fiscal second-quarter profit as its AI profitability and e-commerce business improved.

The Hangzhou-based company has doubled down on artificial intelligence as a growth driver, a push that faces a new risk from heightened scrutiny about exports of chips to China. It has committed to spending more than $53 billion over three years to develop both the hardware and software that power AI.

Its success on that front holds the key to staying competitive amid challenges from other big tech companies and startups alike. But going all in on AI has proved a drag on profitability over recent quarters, putting pressure on Alibaba to deliver on its AI goals.

Its latest results look reassuring.

Alibaba said net profit tripled from a year earlier to 64.535 billion yuan, equivalent to $9.68 billion, for the three months ended September. Analysts polled by FactSet had expected 23.72 billion yuan. Revenue grew about 10% to 271.52 billion yuan, also better than market estimates.

Alibaba said higher net investment income and income from operations drove the profit gains.

The earnings beat comes as the Chinese technology titan prepares a Hong Kong listing for its chip unit, T-Head, that investors view as a major validation of its efforts to produce in-house semiconductors. The business could fetch a valuation of $85 billion, according to Nomura estimates.

Alibaba on Thursday said its new AI chip, Zhenwu V900, is scheduled for commercial release for the first quarter of 2027.

But Alibaba still depends heavily on externally sourced chips, making it potentially vulnerable to tightened export controls. Its stock has fallen about 10% this week since the U.S. move to tighten export rules of advanced American-made chips.

The U.S. said this week that Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and Brazil will be added to a list of countries subject to export restrictions, a step intended to prevent Chinese customers from accessing data-center capacity in those countries remotely.

"We see this as a negative development for China's AI cloud industry, as tighter access to advanced computing resources could constrain AI model training and slow cloud revenue growth," Nomura analysts said in a research note.

Daiwa analyst John Choi said a rerating of China's internet sector is unlikely until investors gain conviction in Alibaba and Tencent, which will likely be the first stocks to be added if investors increase their China exposure. Concerns about Alibaba's elevated AI investment might ease if cloud profitability improves, he wrote in a note ahead of the results.

The company appears to be delivering on that front, with cloud business adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, and amortization more than doubling in the three months ended September, thanks to revenue growth and better operating efficiency. Meanwhile adjusted Ebita for its core e-commerce business more than tripled as losses in the food-delivery business narrowed.

Alibaba Cloud's recurring revenue from external customers rose 67%, driving faster overall cloud revenue growth, with profitability improving significantly, the company said.

Adjusted net profit--a metric closely watched by analysts, as it reflects core business operation profitability--rose 92% to 19.91 billion yuan. The measure excludes the effects of share-based compensation expenses, investment gains and losses, some impairments and other items.

"As AI monetization continues to ramp up, we will maintain disciplined investments in AI capabilities with a focus on return on invested capital while targeting to achieve positive free cash flow," Chief Financial Officer Toby Xu said.

E-commerce business revenue rose 2% in the second quarter. Revenue from AI cloud and compute services jumped 53%, while AI labs and applications revenue climbed 51%.

Write to Tracy Qu at tracy.qu@wsj.com

Malaysian palm oil futures ended more than 1% lower on Thursday, extending losses to a third consecutive session, as Dalian palm olein tumbled on record high inventories in China.

The benchmark palm oil contract for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange slid 54 ringgit, or 1.23%, to 4,332 ringgit ($1,053.25) a metric ton at the close.

The market came under heavy selling pressure in tandem with weakness in Dalian palm olein and soyoil as bearish sentiment swept across the broader edible oil complex, a Kuala Lumpur-based trader said.

Anilkumar Bagani, head of research at vegetable oil broker Sunvin Group, said that the selloff in Dalian palm olein futures has been staggering this week as the market is feeling the heat from the historically high palm oil stocks there.

"Prices are under pressure too as the narrowing discount against gasoil threatens demand for palm oil in biofuel production," he said.

Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) fell 1.43%, while its palm oil contract shed 3.01%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade were up 0.62%.

Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.

Oil prices edged up following losses in the prior session as worries about Middle East supplies amid attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz pushed up against expectations for a market surplus. O/R

Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.

The ringgit , palm's currency of trade, strengthened 0.05% against the dollar, making the commodity slightly expensive for buyers holding foreign currencies.

($1 = 4.1130 ringgit)

data.title: UK's FTSE 100 slips to six-week low as defensive stocks drag
data.description:
Britain's FTSE 100 index hit a six-week low on Thursday, pressured by losses in defensive heavyweights including Unilever, National Grid and AstraZeneca, while investors awaited Anthropic's hotly anticipated Nasdaq debut.

The blue-chip FTSE 100 CURRENCYCOM:UK100 fell 0.3% to 10,522.96 points as of 1111 GMT. The midcap FTSE 250 index ticked down 0.1% to 24,328.34, set for its sixth consecutive session of declines.

  • Anthropic is set to begin trading under the ticker ANT later on Thursday after pricing its upsized IPO above marketed range, valuing the company at about $1.5 trillion

  • UK stocks lagged a tech-led rally in Europe, with optimism around Anthropic's market debut doing little to buoy the domestic market

  • "(If) investors become more enthused with tech, non-tech indices like the FTSE 100 will come under stress, which could lead to further losses if the post-Anthropic optimism is sustained," Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB, said

  • Defensive corners of the market were the main drag: Among consumer staples Unilever fell 2.1%, and British American Tobacco dropped 1.7%; National Grid dropped 2.5% and AstraZeneca lost 1.1%

  • Limiting declines, industrial metal miners (.FTNMX551020) rose 1.1% to recover from their biggest one-day decline since April 4 in the previous session, as copper prices rebounded nearly 0.8%

  • Anglo American , Antofagasta and Glencore rose more than 1%

  • Precious metal miners gained nearly 1%, supported by a rebound in gold prices after they hit a 14-month low in the previous session

  • Markets will also be watching developments around a proposed UK-EU "trusted partnership", seen as key to securing 'Made in Europe' status for British vehicles

  • In company news, Babcock International jumped 7% to the top of the FTSE 100 after the defence engineering group posted a 13% increase in first-half underlying operating profit

  • Merchant banking group Close Brothers slid 7% to lead midcap decliners after the lender said it expects a further modest decline in net interest margin for the rest of fiscal year 2027

data.title: Temu-owner PDD misses third-quarter revenue estimates
data.description:
Temu-owner PDD Holdings missed Wall Street estimates for third-quarter revenue on Thursday, weighed by intense competition in China and regulatory pressure overseas.

The company posted revenue of 108.3 billion yuan ($16.25 billion) for the quarter, compared with analysts' average estimate of 115.97 billion yuan, according to data compiled by LSEG.

data.title: Europe's gas squeeze set to linger into 2027
data.description:
Key points:
  • STOXX 600 up 0.1%
  • Tech leads gains, defensives lag
  • Anthropic debuts on Nasdaq
  • Nasdaq futures rise 2.1%

EUROPE'S GAS SQUEEZE SET TO LINGER INTO 2027

Europe's ban on Russian LNG imports from January 2027 is set to tighten an already strained gas market and keep TTF prices supported into this winter, BCA Research says.

Russian LNG accounts for about 6.3% of EU gas supply, and replacing those volumes will come at a cost, it says, with Qatari supply still disrupted, Norwegian flows near capacity and limited scope for Algeria or Libya to fill the gap.

That leaves US LNG as the only source large enough to offset the loss, but that increases competition with Asian buyers for cargoes.

Still, BCA sees relief from the second quarter of 2027 as Middle East exports recover, US capacity expands and seasonal demand eases. For investors, its strategists recommend "selling natural gas into strength in the coming months."
